examples.en: The survey results are analyzed in a table.
The cause has not been analyzed yet.
We held a meeting after looking at the analyzed data.
The sample will be analyzed tomorrow.

examples.ko: 이 사고는 여러 가지로 분석되고 있어요.
examples.en: This accident is being analyzed in several ways.
The data was analyzed and came out as a graph.

explain: '분석하다'는 사람이 하는 일이고, '분석되다'는 결과나 자료가 주인공일 때 써요. 뉴스, 보고서, 연구 글에서 자주 나와요. '결과가 분석되다'처럼 말하면 누가 했는지는 말하지 않아요.
explain_en: Use the active verb when a person does the analyzing, and this passive form when the data or result is the subject. It shows up in news, reports, and research writing, and it leaves out who did the work.

examples.en: This is the only bakery in the neighborhood.
My only hobby is photography.

examples.ko: 유일하게 그 사람만 제 말을 믿었어요.
examples.en: He was the only one who believed me.
This method might be the only one.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 우리 집의 유일한 손자예요.
examples.en: That child is our family's only grandson.
It is precious because it is one of a kind.

explain: '유일하다'는 주로 '유일한 + 명사' 모양으로 써요. '하나뿐인'이라고 말하는 일상 표현보다 조금 딱딱하게 들려요. '유일하게'는 부사처럼 '그 사람만'이라는 느낌을 줘요.
explain_en: It mostly appears as a modifier before a noun. It sounds a little more formal than everyday words for 'the only one'. The adverb form carries the feeling of 'only that person'.

examples.en: The company promotes its new product.
I want to promote our club.
City hall publicized the festival yesterday.
I am looking for a way to promote the shop.
Many people promote things on the internet.
I told my friends about it, and customers increased.

explain: '광고하다'는 돈을 내고 알리는 느낌이 강하고, '홍보하다'는 널리 알려서 좋은 이미지를 만든다는 느낌이에요. 회사, 학교, 지역 행사 이야기에서 자주 써요. '홍보 담당', '홍보물'처럼 명사로도 많이 나와요.
explain_en: Compared with the word for paying for an ad, this one stresses spreading information to build a good image. It is common for companies, schools and local events, and the noun form appears in words for PR staff and PR materials.

examples.en: I buy shoes online.
Tickets are cheaper if you buy them in advance.
I purchased a laptop last week.
I wrote the items to buy in a list.
The book I purchased arrived today.
It's on sale, so I'm buying a lot.

explain: 가게에서 말할 때는 '사다'를 훨씬 많이 써요. '구매하다'는 쇼핑몰, 앱, 안내문, 영수증 같은 글에서 자주 보여요. '구매 목록', '구매 후기'처럼 명사로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: In conversation at a shop, the plain verb for buying is far more common. This word is typical of online shops, apps, notices and receipts, and the noun form appears in terms like purchase list and purchase review.

examples.en: This day is commemorated every year.
That event is commemorated at the museum.
Today is a day when the founding is commemorated.

examples.ko: 영웅이 기념될 수 있도록 동상을 세웠어요.
examples.en: They put up a statue so the hero can be remembered.
The commemorated date is written on the calendar.
It was commemorated with an event, so many people came.

explain: 기념일이나 큰 일을 기억하고 축하하는 행사가 있을 때 써요. 사람이 하면 '기념하다', 날이나 사건이 주인이면 '기념되다'예요. 일상 대화에서는 '기념일', '기념품', '기념사진'처럼 명사로 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: Used when a special day or big event is remembered with a ceremony. A person doing it uses the active verb; the day or event as subject takes this passive. In daily talk the noun forms like anniversary, souvenir and commemorative photo are more common.

examples.en: The judges select the book of the year.
The school selected a representative student.
It took time to choose the venue.
We will contact the people we selected.
I want to select just one candidate.

examples.ko: 기준에 맞는 곳을 선정해서 보내 주세요.
examples.en: Please pick places that fit the criteria and send them.

explain: '고르다'는 일상에서 쓰고, '선정하다'는 기준을 세워 공식적으로 뽑을 때 써요. 상, 대회, 공모, 이벤트 결과에서 자주 나와요. 뽑힌 쪽에서는 '선정되다'를 써요.
explain_en: The everyday word for choosing is used casually, while this one fits picking by criteria in an official way, as in awards, contests and event results. The passive form is what the chosen side says.

examples.en: A new method is being tried for the first time.
That experiment was attempted several times.
It is something that has never been tried.
It is planned to be tried next month.
Various approaches are being tried.
Even if it is tried, success is hard.

explain: 새 방법이나 실험을 해 본다는 사실을 말할 때, 해 본 사람을 밝히지 않고 써요. '시도된 적이 없다', '여러 번 시도되다'처럼 자주 써요. 뉴스나 설명하는 글에서 주로 써서 말할 때는 '해 보다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Used to say that a new method or experiment is being tried, without naming who tries it. Phrases like 'has never been tried' and 'was tried several times' are common. It is mostly for news and explanatory writing; in speech, the plain phrase for 'give it a try' sounds more natural.

examples.en: The government builds a new bridge.
That company constructed apartments.
They are looking for land to build a factory.
They are building a park in the city.
It took three years to build.
They built a road, and the village became more convenient.

explain: '짓다'는 집이나 건물을 일상적으로 말할 때 쓰고, '건설하다'는 다리, 도로, 댐, 도시처럼 큰 것을 지을 때 써요. '나라를 건설하다'처럼 사회나 나라를 세운다는 뜻으로도 써요. '건설 회사', '건설 현장'이 자주 쓰여요.
explain_en: The everyday verb for building houses is used casually, while this one fits big things such as bridges, roads, dams and cities. It can also mean founding a nation or society. Construction company and construction site are common phrases.

examples.en: He denies the rumor.
The government denied responsibility.
You cannot deny the fact.
It looked strange that he denied it to the end.
He denied his mistake and got angry.
The company denied it, so the article was corrected.

explain: '아니라고 하다'와 비슷하지만 '부인하다'는 사실이나 혐의를 공식적으로 인정하지 않을 때 써요. 뉴스에서 자주 들려요. 같은 소리의 '부인(아내)'과 헷갈리지 않게 문장 속 쓰임을 보세요.
explain_en: Similar to saying 'it is not so', but this verb is for officially refusing to admit a fact or accusation, and it is common in the news. Do not confuse it with a same-sounding noun that means wife or married woman.

examples.en: I set the phone alarm to seven.
I set a new password.
Do not set your goal too high.
It takes long because there are many items to configure.
The screen I set up has changed.
I use it with the language set to Korean.

explain: 앱과 기계에서는 '설정'이 메뉴 이름으로도 쓰여서 '설정에서 바꾸세요'라고 자주 말해요. 목표나 기준을 정한다는 뜻으로도 써요. '정하다'보다 기계나 공식적인 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: Setting is also the name of the menu in apps and devices, so people often say 'change it in Settings'. It also means to fix a goal or standard. It feels more technical or formal than the plain verb for deciding.

examples.en: The game is postponed because of rain.
The meeting was postponed to next week.
I do not know why the departure was delayed.
The event might be postponed.
The exam keeps being postponed.
The show was postponed, so I changed my ticket.

explain: 사람이 미루면 '연기하다', 일정이 미뤄지면 '연기되다'를 써요. 공지나 뉴스에서 '연기됐습니다'라는 말을 자주 들어요. 연기(演技, 연기하다)와 소리가 같으니 문장으로 구별해요.
explain_en: The active verb is for a person putting something off, and this passive is for a schedule that gets pushed back. It is common in announcements. It sounds the same as a word for acting, so context tells them apart.

en: be put together; be summed up

examples.en: Many opinions are brought together into one.
The survey content was summed up in the report.
It is easy to understand when you look at the combined results.
When all materials are collected, they will be put together.
Each class's scores are being totaled.
The opinions were put together, and the presentation started.

explain: 여러 가지가 모여 하나로 정리될 때 써요. 단순히 숫자를 더하는 '합하다'보다 내용을 정리해서 묶는 느낌이에요. 보고서와 발표, 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Used when many things come together into one organized whole. Unlike simple adding, it suggests sorting content and bundling it. It is common in reports, presentations and the news.

examples.en: The two companies are merged into one.
The apps were integrated into one.
The integrated system is more convenient.
The schools will be merged next year.
Several services are being integrated.
The accounts were merged, so I log in only once.

explain: 따로 있던 것이 하나가 될 때 써요. 회사, 학교, 서비스, 계정 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 짝말은 '분리되다', '나뉘다'예요.
explain_en: Used when separate things become one, as with companies, schools, services and accounts. Its opposite partners are the words for being separated or divided.

examples.en: We merge the two teams into one.
The company merged several sites.
Merging the data is difficult.
Please tell me how to merge the files.
We integrate and manage the services.
I want to integrate all the records.

explain: '합치다'는 일상에서 쓰고, '통합하다'는 조직이나 시스템처럼 큰 것을 하나로 묶을 때 써요. 일하는 곳에서 자주 들어요. 목적어에 '를/을'을 붙여 '무엇을 통합하다'로 써요.
explain_en: The everyday verb for putting things together is casual; this one fits larger things like organizations and systems and is often heard at work. It takes an object, as in 'integrate something'.

examples.en: The medicine stabilizes the patient's condition.
The mother calmed the crying baby.
It is a policy that stabilizes prices.
I need time to calm my mind.

examples.ko: 따뜻한 차가 긴장한 몸을 안정시켜 줘요.
examples.en: Warm tea calms a tense body.
Steady your voice and try to speak.

explain: 사람이나 마음, 상태, 물가 같은 것을 흔들리지 않게 만든다는 말이에요. '안정되다'는 스스로 차분해지는 것이고 '안정시키다'는 누군가가 그렇게 만드는 거예요. '마음을 안정시키다'라고 자주 말해요.
explain_en: This means making a person, mood, condition or price steady. The intransitive partner '안정되다' is about becoming calm by itself, while this one is somebody making it so. 'Calm your mind' is a very common use.

examples.en: Our team plans a new event.
I planned a trip with a friend.
I work planning exhibitions.
We are looking for someone to plan a new program.
The video I planned is very popular.
After planning the event, I made a poster.

explain: '계획하다'는 앞으로 할 일을 정하는 것이고, '기획하다'는 행사, 상품, 방송처럼 새로운 것을 만들려고 아이디어와 틀을 짜는 것에 가까워요. 직업 이름 '기획자'와 '기획서'를 같이 알아 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: The general word for planning is about deciding what to do; this one is closer to designing the concept and structure of a new event, product or show. Useful to know with the job title planner and the word for a proposal document.

examples.en: The cat approaches carefully.
A stranger suddenly approached me.
Try approaching this problem differently.
I can hear a car approaching.
It is dangerous, so you must not get close.

examples.ko: 더 쉽게 접근할 수 있는 방법이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a way to approach it more easily.

explain: 장소로 다가갈 때도 쓰고, 문제를 어떻게 다룰지 말할 때도 써요. '문제에 접근하다'처럼 방법의 뜻이 있어요. '다가가다'는 더 부드럽고 일상적인 말이에요.
explain_en: It works for physically moving closer and also for how you handle a problem, as in 'approach an issue'. The plain verb for coming near sounds softer and more everyday.

examples.en: Photography is prohibited here.
Food is banned in the library.
You must not enter forbidden places.
This drug will be banned from next year.
Parking was prohibited, so I parked elsewhere.
It is a day when swimming is prohibited.

explain: 표지판이나 안내문에서 '금지'라는 글자를 많이 봐요. '금지되다'는 규칙이 있어서 못 하게 되어 있다는 뜻이에요. 누가 막는지 말하지 않고 규칙만 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: You see the noun for prohibition on signs and notices all the time. This passive form states that a rule makes something not allowed, without naming who enforces it.

examples.en: I carry out important work at the company.
The team carried out the mission safely.
I want to perform my role well.
There is not enough time to carry out the assignment.
The result differs depending on who carries it out.
We carried it out as planned and succeeded.

explain: '하다'보다 딱딱하고, 맡은 임무나 과제를 끝까지 해낸다는 느낌이에요. '수행평가'는 학교에서 수업 중 과제를 평가하는 말이에요. 일, 임무, 역할, 과제와 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is stiffer than the plain verb for doing, with a sense of carrying an assigned task through. A related school word names in-class performance assessment. It pairs well with work, mission, role and assignment.

examples.en: That name is often mentioned in the news.
The problem was not mentioned in the meeting.
Please check the mentioned contents again.
This book has been mentioned in many places.
It is scheduled to be mentioned next time.
The singer's name is being mentioned.

explain: '말하다'보다 딱딱하고, 어떤 일을 잠깐 꺼내서 이야기할 때 써요. '언급하다'는 말하는 사람이 주인공이고 '언급되다'는 말해진 내용이 주인공이에요. 뉴스와 글에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Stiffer than the plain verb for saying, it is for bringing something up briefly. The active form has the speaker as subject; this passive has the thing mentioned as subject. It is common in news and writing.

examples.en: I leave a name out of this list.
It is ten thousand won excluding tax.
I excluded spicy food.
There is no reason to exclude him.
We open every day except Sunday.
Calculate after leaving out a few people.

explain: '빼다'는 일상에서 쓰고 '제외하다'는 공식적인 글과 설명에서 써요. '~을/를 제외하고'는 '~만 빼고'라는 뜻으로 아주 자주 나와요. 반대는 '포함하다'예요.
explain_en: The everyday verb for taking out is casual; this one is for formal writing and explanations. The pattern 'excluding X' is very common. Its opposite is the verb for including.

en: let someone take part; enter someone

examples.en: The teacher enters the students in the contest.
I signed my child up for the camp.
I want to let my younger sibling join the game.
We plan to have every class take part in the event.
It costs money to enter a player.
I'm going to submit the form to enter the team.

explain: 다른 사람이 어떤 모임이나 대회에 들어가도록 해 줄 때 써요. 자기가 가는 건 '참가하다'예요. 이 단어는 맡긴 사람, 데려간 사람의 입장에서 말해요.
explain_en: Used when you cause another person to join an event or contest. Going yourself uses the plain participation verb. This one speaks from the viewpoint of the person who arranges it.

examples.en: The two machines communicate with each other.
The spacecraft communicated with Earth.
It is a device that communicates over Wi-Fi.
You cannot communicate in the mountains.
It communicates wirelessly, so no cable is needed.
In the old days, people communicated with signal fires.

explain: 사람끼리 대화하는 '이야기하다'와 달리 기계나 기관이 정보를 주고받을 때 많이 써요. '통신사', '통신비', '통신 장애'처럼 명사 '통신'이 훨씬 자주 보여요.
explain_en: Unlike the verb for chatting, it is mostly used when machines or institutions exchange information. The noun form is much more common, as in phone carrier, phone bill and network outage.

examples.en: On election day I vote at the school.
Our class voted for a favorite song.
I will vote for the first time this time.
The number of people who vote keeps growing.
Opinions differed, so we voted and decided.
We voted with friends and chose a restaurant.

explain: 선거뿐 아니라 친구들끼리 메뉴를 고를 때도 '투표하다'를 가볍게 써요. 누구를 뽑는지 말하려면 '~에게 투표하다'라고 해요. 투표하러 가는 곳은 '투표소'예요.
explain_en: It is not only for elections; friends also use it lightly when choosing a menu. To say who you vote for, use the pattern 'vote for someone'. The place you go to vote is the polling station.

examples.en: I verify myself with the number I got by text.
The government certified this product.
To log in, verify first.
There is an event where you prove it with a photo.
It takes time to authenticate the app.
I post exercise photos as proof.

explain: 인터넷에서 본인 확인을 할 때 '본인 인증'이라고 많이 말해요. '인증샷'은 갔다는 걸 증명하는 사진을 뜻하는 한국어 말이에요. 제품에 '인증 마크'가 붙기도 해요.
explain_en: Online, identity checks are usually called by the noun phrase for self-verification. A Korean term for a proof photo is also built on this word. Products may carry a certification mark.

examples.en: The plan is given up halfway.
That business was finally abandoned.
I took out a dream that had been given up.

examples.ko: 시간이 없으면 일부는 포기될 수 있어요.
examples.en: If time is short, some may be given up.
Several plans are being dropped.
The construction was dropped, so the land is empty.

explain: 계획, 사업, 공사처럼 하던 일이 끝까지 가지 못하고 멈췄을 때 써요. 사람이 스스로 그만두는 건 '포기하다'예요. 일이 멈췄다는 뜻으로 '중단되다'도 많이 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '포기하다'를 훨씬 많이 써요.
explain_en: Used when a plan, business or construction project stops before it is finished. A person quitting by choice uses the active verb. The verb for 'be suspended' is also common for stopped projects. In daily talk the active verb is far more common.

examples.en: I have done business with this bank for a long time.

examples.ko: 두 회사가 십 년 동안 거래했어요.
examples.en: The two companies traded for ten years.

examples.ko: 중고 물건을 직접 만나서 거래하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to meet in person to trade secondhand goods.
There is a way to trade safely.
The shop I deal with has closed.
I paid in cash and got a receipt.

explain: 사고파는 일을 말하는데 가게에서 물건 하나 사는 일에는 잘 안 써요. 회사, 은행, 중고 거래처럼 주고받는 관계가 있을 때 써요. '중고 거래'와 '거래처'를 같이 알아 두세요.
explain_en: It describes buying and selling, but not a single purchase at a shop. It suits ongoing exchanges such as companies, banks and secondhand deals. Learn it with the words for secondhand trade and business partner.

examples.en: A good environment helps a child grow.
That experience made me grow.
I want to grow the company big.
I am looking for ways to develop my skills.
Sunlight is important for growing plants.
They grew a small shop into a chain.

explain: '자라다'는 스스로 크는 것이고 '성장시키다'는 누군가가 키우거나 발전시키는 것이에요. 회사, 실력, 경제처럼 추상적인 것에도 써요. 사람이 크는 일은 '키우다'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: The intransitive verb is growing by itself; this one is making something grow or develop. It works for abstract things like a company, skill or economy. For raising children, the plain verb for raising is more common.

examples.en: He is a just police officer.
I want to build a just society.
The way they helped their friend is righteous.
Acting justly is not easy.
I think a person looks coolest when they are righteous.
He is just, so many people trust and follow him.

explain: '정의'에 '-롭다'가 붙은 말로 ㅂ 불규칙이라 '정의로워요', '정의로운'으로 바뀌어요. 사람이나 행동, 사회를 칭찬할 때 써요. 일상 대화보다 글이나 영화 이야기에서 더 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Built from the noun for justice plus a suffix, it is a b-irregular adjective, so it becomes the forms ending in 'wo'. It praises people, actions and societies, and shows up more in writing and movie talk than in daily chat.

examples.en: A new rule is proposed at the meeting.
Several solutions were suggested.
The proposed date is Friday.
A better method will be proposed.
Ideas keep being suggested.
The plan was proposed, and we started right away.

explain: 회의에서 의견이나 계획이 나왔을 때, 낸 사람을 밝히지 않고 써요. 제안을 들은 쪽은 '제안을 받다'라고 해요. 회의록, 기사, 보고서에서 많이 나오고, 말할 때는 '제안하다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: Used when an opinion or plan comes up at a meeting, without naming who put it forward. The side that hears the proposal says 'receive a proposal'. It appears in minutes, articles and reports; in speech, the active verb sounds more natural.

examples.en: People's attention is focused on one place.
The population is concentrated in Seoul.

examples.ko: 힘이 한 사람에게 집중되면 문제가 생겨요.
examples.en: When power is concentrated in one person, problems arise.
Everyone's eyes were on one person.
It is news that will draw attention.
All eyes were on me, so I felt a little shy.

explain: '집중하다'는 사람이 하는 일이고 '집중되다'는 관심, 시선, 인구, 힘이 한쪽에 모일 때 써요. '관심이 집중되다', '시선이 집중되다'가 자주 쓰는 짝이에요.
explain_en: The active form is a person focusing; this passive is for attention, gazes, population or power gathering in one place. 'Attention is focused' and 'gazes are focused' are the usual pairs.

examples.en: The teacher gets the students to focus.
An interesting story held the audience's attention.

examples.ko: 조용한 음악이 학생들의 주의를 집중시켜 줘요.
examples.en: Quiet music helps focus the students' attention.
I need a way to get a child to focus.
I will focus the effort in one place.
I clapped first to get their attention.

explain: 다른 사람의 주의나 힘을 한곳으로 모으게 할 때 써요. 자기가 집중하는 건 '집중하다'예요. 수업이나 발표에서 '집중시키다'가 자주 쓰여요.
explain_en: Used when you make other people's attention or effort gather in one spot. Focusing yourself uses the plain verb. It is common in class and presentation contexts.

examples.en: The players train every morning.
I trained the puppy.
Soldiers are training even in the snow.
The training time is long, so it is tiring.
I need a friend to practice speaking with.
We trained hard and won the competition.

explain: '연습하다'보다 규칙적이고 엄격한 느낌이 있어요. 운동선수, 군인, 동물을 가르칠 때 많이 써요. 훈련을 받는 쪽은 '훈련을 받다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It feels more regular and strict than simple practice. It is common for athletes, soldiers and animal training. The trainee side says 훈련을 받다 (receive training).

examples.en: The king gives an order to his servant.
The boss ordered us to finish the work quickly.
Do not give me orders.
I do not like the commanding tone.
The general will order the soldiers to move.
He gave the order and left.

explain: '시키다'가 일상에서 쓰는 말이라면 '명령하다'는 지위가 위인 사람이 강하게 시킬 때 써요. 군대, 왕, 법원 이야기에서 나오고 친구 사이에서는 좀 세게 들려요. 컴퓨터의 '명령어'도 같은 말이에요.
explain_en: The everyday word for telling someone to do something is milder; this one is a person of higher rank giving a strong order, as in military, royal or court contexts. Among friends it sounds harsh. Computer commands use the same root.

examples.en: The incident is reported in the news.
The news of the accident was reported in the morning.
What was reported turned out not to be true.
It will be reported in tomorrow's newspaper.
News about the typhoon keeps being reported.

examples.ko: 크게 보도돼서 많은 사람이 알게 됐어요.
examples.en: It was widely reported, so many people found out.

explain: 방송과 신문이 사건을 알릴 때 쓰는 말이에요. 기자나 방송사가 주인이면 '보도하다', 소식이 주인이면 '보도되다'예요. '보도 자료'는 기관이 기자들에게 주는 글이에요.
explain_en: Used when the press announces an event. With a reporter or broadcaster as subject it is the active verb; with the news as subject it is this passive. A press release is the related noun phrase.

examples.en: The stain is removed cleanly.
Ads were removed from the app.

examples.ko: 제거된 파일은 다시 볼 수 없어요.
examples.en: Removed files cannot be seen again.
I wait until the danger is removed.
Harmful germs are being eliminated.
The problem was eliminated, so I feel at ease.

explain: 더럽거나 위험하거나 필요 없는 것이 없어질 때 써요. '없어지다'보다 방법이 있어서 사라졌다는 느낌이 있어요. 짝말은 '제거하다'와 '추가되다'예요.
explain_en: Used when something dirty, dangerous or unneeded disappears. It suggests removal by some method, more than simply vanishing. Related words are the active verb and the passive of adding.

examples.en: The chairperson starts the meeting.

examples.ko: 우리 학교 위원장은 삼 학년 학생이에요.
examples.en: The head of our school committee is a third-year student.
We elected a new chairperson yesterday.
I will tell the chairperson first.
That person works as the head of the election committee.
Applause came after the chairperson finished speaking.

explain: 위원회의 가장 높은 사람의 직함이라서 '위원장님'처럼 '님'을 붙여 불러요. 회사는 '사장', 학교는 '교장'처럼 조직마다 책임자 이름이 달라요. 그 아래 자리는 '부위원장'이에요.
explain_en: It is the title of the top person in a committee, so people add the honorific suffix when addressing the person. The head of a company or school has a different title, such as the words for president or principal. The position below is the vice chair.

examples.en: The teacher applies a new rule.
I applied the grammar I learned to speaking.

examples.ko: 할인은 모든 상품에 적용할 수 없어요.
examples.en: The discount cannot be applied to every item.

examples.ko: 이 방법을 일에 적용해 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to try applying this method at work.
I applied the coupon and then paid.
The newly applied system is complicated.

explain: 규칙, 방법, 쿠폰, 이론을 실제 상황에 쓸 때 써요. 영어 apply에는 지원한다는 뜻이 있지만 '적용하다'는 지원서를 내는 뜻이 아니에요. 지원할 때는 '지원하다'를 써요.
explain_en: Used for putting a rule, method, coupon or theory into real use. Unlike the English word 'apply', it does not mean applying for a job; that uses the separate verb for applying.
